title_en: How Long Does It Take in Chinese

sentences.en: I was planning to visit a friend over the weekend — he lives in another city.
I went to the train station and asked the clerk: "How long does it take to get there by train?"
The clerk said, "On the fast train it's two hours."
I bought a Saturday morning train ticket.
The train went really fast — I read for a while on the train, then looked at my phone for a while.
Only two hours had passed, and the train had really arrived.
When I came out, my friend was already waiting at the door, and said I'd arrived just in time.

quiz.q: What does the narrator ask the train station clerk?
According to the clerk, how long does the trip take with no traffic?
What does the friend say when the narrator arrives?
a: That the trip took too long
That the narrator arrived just in time

grammar.p: 要多长时间？(How long does it take?)
grammar.e: 多长时间 asks about duration — how long something takes — while 多远 asks about distance instead.
grammar.x: 坐火车去，要多长时间？— How long does it take to get there by train?

grammar.p: 才 + time period（only; not until — something is less than expected）
grammar.e: 才 before a time expression emphasizes that only that much time had passed, showing it felt quick.
grammar.x: 才过了两个小时，火车真的到了。— Only two hours had passed, and the train had really arrived.

grammar.p: V + 得 + adjective（complement describing how an action turned out）
grammar.e: 来得正好 uses 得 to attach a description of the result — arriving right on time.
grammar.x: 朋友已经在门口等我了，说我来得正好。— My friend was already waiting at the door, and said I'd arrived just in time.
